blocks.text: On Friday afternoon, Mrs. Evans, was going out she took her handbag and umbrella, pulled the door behind her to lock it and went to the Ladies’s Club. She always goes there on Fridays.

When she came back home, she went into the living room and at once smelled cigarette smoke. She never smoked. “Had somebody broken in?” she thought. She checked all doors and windows. They were all locked. She went from room to room checking. She noticed that some things were missing.

She wondered whether someone might have a key that fitted her front door. She decided to stay at home the following Friday. Nothing happened. Perhaps someone was watching her movements. On the Friday after that, she went out as usual but instead of going to the Club she took a short cut home again and entered the house through the backdoor. She waited in the kitchen. While she was making a cup of tea, she heard a sound coming from the door. Suddenly, she saw a long piece of wire entering through the letter-box and then a hand. She had the tea kettle with boiling water in her hand. She raised it and poured the water over the hand. There was a shout outside. The wire fell to the floor, the hand was pulled back, and she heard the sound of hurrying feet running away.
She reported the episode to the police that same evening. They came and took the wire away. A few days later the police found the man and recovered Mrs. Evans’ things.
Write a sentence about each picture:

items.q: What did Mrs. Evans usually do on Friday afternoon?
What kind of smell was there in the living room when she got in?
Was she a smoker?
What did she notice?
What did she decide to do the following Friday?
What happened while she was making a cup of tea?
What did she see coming through the letter-box?
What did she do then?
Did she call the police that evening?
When did the police find the man?

blocks.text: While Mr. Brown was getting the car out of the garage his wife went round the house closing all the windows and turning off the lights. They were going to a concert that evening.

items: *Mr. Brown:* Did you close all the windows and lock the front door, dear?
*Mrs. Brown:* Why do you ask? I certainly did. You know there have been a lot of burglaries in this neighborhood lately.
*Mr. Brown:* And the police haven’t done much about it. Thieves seem to be very clever, in these days, more clever than the cops, I would say.
*Mrs. Brown:* Fortunately, our house is well protected and it won’t be easy to get in. By the way, do you have the tickets?
*Mr. Brown:* Who me? I thought you’d taken them from the cupboard. Oh, no. Don’t tell me you don’t have them.
*Mrs. Brown:* Well, I’m afraid we’ll have to go back home for the tickets.
*Mr. Brown:* Please turn on the dining-room lights, I can’t find them in the dark.
*Mrs. Brown:* Look! What’s that bag on the floor? And that window is open!
*Mr. Brown:* Gee, somebody broke in while we were going to the theater. My dear, I’m afraid you didn’t close that window, after all.
*Mrs. Brown:* How could it have happened? I was quite sure I had. Let’s see if there’s something missing. I can’t believe it. He couldn’t take anything away.
*Mr. Brown:* I think he saw the lights of the car outside. Then he realized that if he wanted to run away he wouldn’t be able to take anything with him.
*Mrs. Brown:* We were lucky we left the tickets behind, otherwise that uninvited guest would have gotten away with it.

items.q: What was Mrs. Brown doing?
Was Mr. Brown in the house?
Why did they have to be exceptionally careful about doors and windows?
What did Mr. Brown complain about?
Why did they have to go back to their house?
How did the burglar break into the house?
Why did he run away?

rows: I’m worried about Mrs. Evans. I haven’t seen her for a week.
You shouldn’t worry. You know she often stays with her daughter.
There are strange noises inside the house. I’m scared to death.
Just keep cool and call the police.
It was a really frightening experience.
